text: Rate-limit wrapped-agent control effects per socket connection
description: Add deterministic per-connection token-bucket budgets after payload validation and before capability-bearing effects. Use separate budgets suited to interaction shape: terminal input burst 200/refill 100 per second, resize burst/refill 30 per second, and watchdog toggles burst 5/refill 1 per second. Share each category across worker/watchdog variants so alternating event names cannot multiply capacity. Drop over-budget events without calling WatchdogService, Agent.write, Agent.resize, or creating repaint timers; recover predictably with injected monotonic time. Add unit tests for burst limits, refill, clock rollback, category isolation/shared variants, and zero-effect rejection. Do not launch or restart servers.

reflections.context: Per-event socket validation bounded shape and size, but an allowed-origin client could still emit unlimited valid PTY writes, resize repaint sequences/timers, or watchdog state toggles. Worker/watchdog variants used separate event names that could otherwise multiply any naive per-handler limit.
reflections.outcome: Added one deterministic token-bucket limiter per Socket.IO connection with shared categories across worker/watchdog variants: terminal input capacity 200/refill 100 per second, resize 30/30, and watchdog toggle 5/1. Validation occurs first; only canonical valid payloads consume category capacity. Over-budget events return before WatchdogService, PTY writes, resizes, or repaint timers. Time is injectable, capacities are clamped, and backward clock movement grants no tokens.
reflections.effectiveness: Five focused limiter tests cover exact burst rejection, refill/capacity clamping, clock rollback recovery, category isolation with shared variant budget, and zero terminal effects after exhaustion. The complete wrapped-agents/common suite passes 185/185 tests, TypeScript tsc --noEmit passes, and git diff --check passes. The first verification also caught and corrected a test-only Array.at incompatibility with the package's configured TS lib. No server or session was launched or restarted.
reflections.lesson: Bounding individual messages is not enough for an availability-sensitive control plane; aggregate effect rate is a separate capability. Apply rate accounting after validation so malformed traffic cannot consume legitimate capacity, and share budgets across aliases of the same effect.
reflections.pattern: Use per-connection, per-capability token buckets with injected monotonic time and test effect absence—not just limiter return values—at exhaustion.

status.comment: Per-connection rate limits now bound all capability-bearing socket effects with shared worker/watchdog category budgets; 185/185 common tests pass. Awaiting explicit user acceptance before done.

valueRationale: An allowed client can otherwise turn individually valid control events into unbounded PTY work, repaint timers, and state churn, undermining availability of the human control plane.
